CHOICE: 1
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 1's char-5 counterexample checks out in outline. The diagonal $\mathbb{Z}/5$-action on $E\times C$ is free because translation by a 5-torsion point on $E$ is free. So $X$ is an étale quotient of $E\times C$, which gives $\kappa(X)=\kappa(E\times C)=1$, so $X$ is not abelian. The invariant-section counts $P_1=P_2=1$ also work out. I did not fully verify $h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)=2$, since the Hochschild–Serre differential for the wild cyclic group could change that count. Solutions 2 and 3 rest on claims about characteristic 3 and 5 that I could not support. The answer 7 also fits the natural pattern "birational to abelian unless $p\in\{2,3,5\}$", but I could not confirm that against the literature.
